pageTitle: Standards reference for Security Hub CSPM
whatThePageStates: This is a short parent/landing page that defines what a 'security standard' is in AWS Security Hub CSPM and then enumerates, in a single bulleted list introduced by 'Security Hub CSPM currently supports the following standards:', the eight standards the service supports. Each bullet is a bolded standard name followed by a prose description of who authored it and what it covers; there is no table, no column of Yes/No values, and no per-Region or per-plan qualification anywhere on the page. Two paragraphs of caveat follow (standards do not guarantee regulatory compliance; individual controls can belong to more than one standard, and consolidated control findings deduplicate findings across standards). A 'Topics' block then repeats the same eight items as navigation links to child pages, and a 'See also' block carries generic AI-coding-assistant boilerplate. The only coverage claim on the page is the positive list of supported standards; nothing is stated as unsupported.

features.featureName: Security standards supported by Security Hub CSPM
features.statuses: 8 supported (Yes), 0 not supported, 0 partial; 8+0+0=8. Counting the bullets under 'Security Hub CSPM currently supports the following standards:': (1) AWS Foundational Security Best Practices, (2) AI Security Best Practices, (3) AWS Resource Tagging, (4) CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark, (5) NIST SP 800-53 Revision 5, (6) NIST SP 800-171 Revision 2, (7) PCI DSS, (8) Service-managed standard, AWS Control Tower. Every entry is an affirmative support statement carried by the list's lead-in sentence; the page never writes 'No', 'not supported', 'isn't available', or any exclusion note, so there are zero stated negatives and zero tri-state/Partial values. Absence of a standard (for example ISO 27001, HIPAA, SOC 2, GDPR) is silence, not a claim of non-support.
features.scope: None. The page attaches no second dimension to any standard: no Region availability, no partition, no pricing tier or plan, no per-account/per-Organization qualifier, and no version qualifier. 'CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark' is named without any of its versions (v1.2.0/v1.4.0/v3.0.0), and 'Service-managed standard, AWS Control Tower' is named without listing which Control Tower controls it covers; both are single undifferentiated entries here.
features.reasoning: The axis is the thing enumerated by the one list on the page, and that thing is a set of named security standards that Security Hub publishes about itself — a catalogue, not an externally existing universe such as Regions or services. The unit of claim is one standard, because that is the granularity at which the lead-in sentence asserts support and at which each child page is written. Rows do not collapse: each of the 8 bullets names a distinct standard, so expectedCount equals the number of distinct axis values and distinctTargets/collapse are omitted. The controls that make up each standard are explicitly out of scope of this page ('Each standard includes multiple controls' is a definition, not an enumeration) and are counted on the child pages instead.

shouldNotExtract: The 'Topics' block is site navigation, not a coverage claim — it repeats the same eight items (with 'Service-managed standards' pluralised as a category page), and harvesting both blocks would double the count to 16. The 'See also' block about 'Skills for AI coding assistants (optional)' and the 'aws agent-toolkit search-skills' command is boilerplate present on every page in this doc set and states no coverage. The opening definition paragraph ('a security standard is a set of requirements ... Each standard includes multiple controls') is conceptual, as is the disclaimer paragraph that standards 'don't guarantee compliance with any regulatory frameworks or audits'. The consolidated-control-findings paragraph is behavioural guidance about finding deduplication, not coverage, and its worked example ('if you enable two standards and a control applies to both ... you receive two separate findings') must not be read as counts. Prose inside the AI Security Best Practices bullet naming 'network isolation, encryption, VPC placement, and AWS KMS key usage' is illustrative domain text, not an enumerated axis. The inline links (controls-findings-create-update.md, the eight child .md links, the agent-toolkit URL) are references, not values.
coverageDimensions: REGION: the page gives nothing. It never names a Region, never mentions Region availability or partitions (no aws-us-gov / aws-cn discussion), and does not say any standard is limited to a subset of Regions. Any per-Region number attributed to this page is fabricated. SERVICE: the page gives nothing enumerable. It names AWS Security Hub CSPM as the service that publishes the standards, and mentions AWS Control Tower and AWS KMS only inside descriptive prose; there is no list of AWS services that the standards assess, and the CIS bullet explicitly says only 'a subset of AWS services and resources' without naming them. RESOURCE TYPE: the page gives nothing. No resource type is named or enumerated; 'AWS resources' and 'deployed AI resources' appear only as generic prose. The single dimension this page actually supplies is the list of 8 supported compliance standards.
trap: The single most likely misparse is double counting: the eight standards appear twice on the page — once as the substantive bulleted list and again as the 'Topics' navigation list — so a parser that harvests every '+' bullet returns 16 instead of 8. Runners-up: (a) treating the second list's 'Service-managed standards' (plural category page) as a ninth distinct standard alongside the first list's 'Service-managed standard, AWS Control Tower', when they are the same entry; (b) inventing negatives — the page states no 'No' values at all, so reporting any not-supported count, or reading the omission of ISO 27001/HIPAA/SOC 2 as a stated exclusion, invents a claim; (c) expanding standards into versions (CIS v1.2.0/v1.4.0/v3.0.0, or PCI DSS v3.2.1/v4.0.1) that this page never lists; (d) drilling into the child .md links and attributing their control counts to this page, which enumerates standards only, never controls; (e) mining the 'See also' AI-coding-assistant boilerplate or the consolidated-findings example paragraph for numbers.
